body:
#2027 (BUG-1442) APPROVED at 53a138232061, hold cleared. Build will need to be green before you merge; I have not checked it yet. Prior round hand-carried into the verdict per the BUG-1539 mitigation — I saved PR-2027.json before recording this time.

IT SATISFIES THE DRAIN REVIEWER'S FINDING AT THE SEAM IT NAMED. The ask was to parse both relationship sections and compare typed edges rather than searching each output for substrings. All four parts are present and I verified them from the diff rather than the commit message: both surfaces parsed into (type, target) pairs, the deliberate vocabulary difference DECLARED in canonical_edge_type rather than assumed, assert_eq! comparing the two projections, and the blocker-state assertions left untouched so they fail independently.

THE DESIGN CLOSES A HOLE THE FINDING DID NOT NAME, and it is the same shape as the defect being fixed: comparing the two projections can pass VACUOUSLY, because if neither parser finds its section both return empty and empty equals empty. The second assertion — the expected edge set pinned, each edge against its own target — is what makes the first one mean anything. An agreement test that passes on two empty results is the substring test's failure mode in different clothes.

THE MOST VALUABLE LINE IN THE COMMIT IS NOT ABOUT THIS PR. Product reports three mutations against the production emitter, all red. I cannot run mutations from this seat, so that is their evidence and I labelled it as theirs. But they also disclosed this:

    TWO OF THOSE MUTATIONS INITIALLY REPORTED GREEN AND NEITHER GREEN MEANT ANYTHING.
    One swap was applied inside the row loop, so three relationships swapped twice and
    cancelled out; the retry missed its anchor on an indentation miscount.

Their rule from it: a mutation that produces green must be shown to have actually changed behaviour before the green is evidence, otherwise "the test did not catch it" and "the code was never changed" are indistinguishable. That is a null-result-that-lies INSIDE THE MUTATION HARNESS — the instrument we have been treating all night as the implementer's half of falsification. It is the third distinct way a green can lie, alongside truncated output and a swallowed exit code, and unlike those two it corrupts evidence we have been relying on rather than evidence we were reading carelessly. If that belongs anywhere durable it is next to the self-falsification material, not on BUG-1442.

ONE THING I RELAYED BUT DID NOT VERIFY, flagged as such in the verdict. They report that above five relationships and without --rels, the human surface prints a COUNT while TOON still enumerates — a live instance of the "extra collapsed rows" divergence, in the PRODUCT rather than the test. Keeping the fixture at three so the test measures what it claims is the right call for this spec. I TRIED TO CONFIRM THE COLLAPSE RULE IN THE RENDERER AND COULD NOT FIND IT — my greps for the Relations section emitter did not surface it, and I stopped rather than keep digging on something my verdict does not depend on. So this is their observation, not my finding. Raising it because if it is real it is a larger defect than the test gap this PR closes, and because a product divergence disclosed only in a commit message reaches git history but never reaches a backlog. Your call whether it earns a spec; I am not filing.

BUG-1550 DID NOT RECUR: I grepped the diff for removed lines carrying /// or trace: and found none, so no existing header was displaced by the four nested functions this commit adds.
subject: #2027 approved at 53a1382320 — plus a THIRD way a green lies, disclosed by product: a mutation that never changed behaviour
